classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the preceding six-canister investigation to seven and choose a compact arrangement without a prescribed construction. The new one-plus-six tangent configuration requires visual/geometric strategy selection, supported by the previous packing cases; the task does not demand an extremal proof.

content.prompt:
The cylindrical canisters have radius $2.5\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$. They must be packaged in one layer with tight shrink-wrap.

Instead of being packaged in bundles of six, the company now decides to package the canisters in bundles of seven. How should the canisters be packed so as to minimise the volume?

answer.short: Place one canister in the centre and six around it, each touching the centre canister and its two neighbours.
answer.worked: Use a central canister with six surrounding canisters. The surrounding centres form a regular hexagon of side $5$ cm. This compact arrangement leaves only the small triangular gaps between neighbouring circles. The tight wrapping follows six straight tangents joined by circular arcs.

spec.description: One central circle with six tangent surrounding circles and a tight rounded-hexagon envelope.
spec.mathematics: All seven circles have equal radius; neighbouring outer centres and the centre are separated by two radii.
